title: Accuracy Management Under Pressure
tagline: Year 4 — Keeping accuracy high at speed: error types, quick checks, and the trade-off between attempts and accuracy

introduction.overview: Score equals correct answers, and correct answers equal attempts times accuracy. Raising attempts by 10% while accuracy falls by 10% lowers your score. Accuracy under pressure is protected by recognising your typical error types (misreading, arithmetic slip, wrong formula, wrong option marked) and by cheap checks: re-reading the question stem, checking units, and a last-digit test. The aim is the point where an extra check costs less than the errors it prevents.
introduction.placementRelevance: Negative marking and sectional cutoffs make accuracy as important as speed.
introduction.realWorldContext: Error-checking habits matter in any accuracy-critical work.

learningObjectives: Compute accuracy and score from attempts
Use cheap checks (units, stem, last digit)

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Accuracy = correct ÷ attempted. Score = correct (− penalty × wrong).

coreDefinitions: Accuracy: correct as a share of attempted.
Misreading error: answering a different question.
Marking error: the right answer, wrong option.
Check budget: seconds per question for verification.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A wrong answer costs the marks plus the time it took; prevention is cheaper.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Read the stem twice, write only what you need, check units and last digit, mark the option carefully.

mainNarrative: A candidate attempts 28 and gets 24 right: accuracy 85.7%. Another attempts 32 with 75% accuracy and gets 24 right: the same score, but more risk with negative marking.
If the penalty is 0.25 per wrong, the first scores 24 − 1 = 23 and the second 24 − 2 = 22.
A 10-second check on each question that prevents 1 error in 20 saves 0.05 × (1 + 0.25) marks, about 0.06 per question; whether it is worth it depends on the time value.
Classify errors after each mock: misreads, slips, formula errors and marking errors need different fixes.
A quick last-digit check catches many slips for a few seconds.

deepDiveAspects.title: Accuracy targets
deepDiveAspects.content: Many aspirants aim for 85–90% accuracy on attempted questions; set your own from your mocks.

deepDiveAspects.title: Pressure effect
deepDiveAspects.content: Errors cluster late in a section; double-check marking near the end.

solvedExamples.title: Trade-off
solvedExamples.question: A: 26 attempts at 90% accuracy. B: 32 attempts at 75%. Which has more correct answers?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: B has slightly more correct answers

solvedExamples.title: Penalty
solvedExamples.question: B (32 attempts, 24 correct, 8 wrong) with penalty 0.25. Score?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Read the stem twice, check units and last digit, and mark options carefully; track error types after each mock.

placementTips.recruiterInsight: A habit of two quick checks beats a habit of re-solving.
